description.para: The following constants map to the XPAR parameters created in the xparameters.h file.
They are defined here so that all needed parameters can be changed in one place.
The instances to support the device drivers are global such that they are initialized to zero each time the program runs.

briefdescription.para: The instance of the UartLite Device.

description.para: The following variables are shared between non-interrupt processing and interrupt processing such that they must be global.
The counter determines when the entire buffer has been sent.

briefdescription.para: Performs a minimal test on the UartLite device and driver.

detaileddescription.para: This function is a design example that illustrates how to use the XUartLite component.
This function sends data through the UartLite.
This function uses the interrupt driver mode of the UartLite. The calls to the UartLite driver in the interrupt handlers, should only use the non-blocking calls.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the instance of UartLite driver.

simplesect.para:
- In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.
This function contains an infinite loop such that if interrupts are not working it may never return.

briefdescription.para: Handles the send complete interrupt event.

detaileddescription.para: This function is called from an interrupt context such that the amount of processing performed should be minimized. It is called when the transmit FIFO of the UartLite is empty and more data can be sent through the UartLite.
This handler provides an example of how to handle data for the UartLite, but is application specific.

parameterdescription.para: Callback reference from the driver. In this case it is the instance pointer for the UartLite driver.
Number of bytes sent or received for sent and receive events.

briefdescription.para: Handles the receive data interrupt event.

detaileddescription.para: This function is called from an interrupt context such that the amount of processing performed should be minimized. It is called when any data is present in the receive FIFO of the UartLite such that the data can be retrieved from the UartLite. The amount of data present in the FIFO is not known when this function is called.
This handler provides an example of how to handle data for the UartLite, but is application specific.

parameterdescription.para: Callback reference from the driver, in this case it is the instance pointer for the UartLite driver.
Number of bytes sent or received for sent and receive events.

briefdescription.para: Demonstrates interrupt-mode transmission with the UartLite driver.
